$comment: Baseline for `pnpm rls:bypass-check` (scripts/check-tenant-bypass.ts).
This is a RATCHET, not a mute button. The gate is red when a key is missing
here (a new bypass), red when a key's count goes UP (a new call site on an
already-known file), and warns when a count goes DOWN (an entry someone fixed
and forgot to remove). `--prune` lowers the counts for you when work lands;
nothing lowers them silently.
kind = 'allowed'       the call site is correct as written and is expected to stay.
kind = 'system-scope'  the call site LEAVES its tenant scope on purpose, through
withSystemScope (src/lib/system-scope.ts), and the reason
is written down. CHECK D counts these.
kind = 'debt'          the call site is wrong; `card` names who closes it. The gate
prints the outstanding debt on every run, green or red, so a
deferred finding cannot go quiet the way the ones in
TASK-MTSHUZUMVLTBF did.
The kind and the check must agree: CHECK D entries are 'system-scope' and no
other check may be. Without that rule the sanctioned path WOULD be the mute
button — moving a call onto withSystemScope takes it out of CHECK A (the
accessor becomes `tx.`), so it has to land in CHECK D or it lands nowhere.
Measured on 2026-09-10 against dev by TASK-MTVTPVTEBCF5Z (slice 6).
Every reason below was read out of the file it names, not inferred from the
path. See docs/agent-results/TASK-MTVTPVTEBCF5Z-de-fb.md.
History: TASK-MTVRAZSUVLL9R recorded 31 'allowed' entries covering 35 call
sites. All 35 were correct as tenant scoping and returned ZERO ROWS under the
NOBYPASSRLS role fabrika_app — measured, not feared. Slice 6 moved them onto
the sanctioned path, where they became 22 call sites in 16 entries: batches
that shared a purpose were collapsed into one scope each (the GDPR export's
six reads, the erasure sweep's eight writes, the digest's two), and one turned
out to be plainly scopable and is now withTenant.
Debt cards, both closed by TASK-MULQKFER4MF0Y (2026-09-29) and pruned:
TASK-MTVTMZXYT84RZ  the two scopable billing calls, now withTenant (K1)
TASK-MTVSBEO7VX6Y4  the subscription-sync fallback, removed by that card

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: The SHA-256 key hash IS the credential and this lookup is what DISCOVERS the tenant, so withTenant cannot wrap it: the argument it needs is this call's result. Measured under fabrika_app: the unscoped read returns no row, so every API key on the platform stops authenticating. The lastUsedAt write that follows is now withTenant(keyRecord.tenantId) — only the read had to cross tenants.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: The Auth.js jwt callback re-reads the signed-in user's memberships on every call (TASK-MUNQB0GR306U0) to put tenantId, role and workspaceIds on the token. This read is what DISCOVERS the tenant, so there is no app.tenant_id to scope it with. Measured under fabrika_app (TASK-MUPYHVSBW47GD#auth, live Supabase): the unscoped read returned zero Membership rows, so every session was tenantless and every user landed on /no-workspace with no role. The read stays bound to the user: User by id, and the memberships relation filter is "Membership"."userId" = token.id, plus the existing tenant.deletedAt and bound/requested-tenant filters. A failure still leaves the token tenantless (fail closed).

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: Magic-token partner portal: there is no session at all. The token is the credential and the row names its own tenant. Two call sites, generateMetadata and the page body, both reading the same row by magicTokenHash (SHA-256 of the URL token, TASK-MULQLL2T8ZJX4). Same discovery shape as api-auth.ts.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: Tenant invitation accept (TASK-MUN2793A57Z9I): lookupInvitation() reads the Invitation row by tokenHash (SHA-256 of the e-mailed token, TASK-MULQLL2T8ZJX4). The token is the credential and the row names its own tenant; the person accepting has no membership in it yet (or no account at all), so there is no tenant to scope to. Same discovery shape as the partner portal. Everything after the read — the conditional acceptedAt UPDATE, Membership, AuditEvent, Consent — runs in withTenant(invitation.tenantId) or a transaction bound to it.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: addBudgetLineByToken. The comment on the line says it: 'Resolved by token, then re-scoped to that row's own tenant for the write.' The read discovers the tenant; savePartContent(part.tenantId, ...) that follows is scoped.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: Answers 'which tenant does this signed-in user own?'. Scoped by session.user.id and role; the tenantId it returns is what createPortalSession is then given. Nothing narrower exists to scope to yet.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: findRecorded(): the idempotency lookup by providerEventId, which runs BEFORE the tenant is known — exactly the api-auth.ts shape. Empty under fabrika_app means every Stripe webhook retry is treated as a new sale.

entries.subject: system-scope:subject-scoped
entries.reason: GDPR Art. 15/20 portability export. ONE scope around the whole Promise.all batch, replacing six separate unscoped reads (user, membership, account, evaluation, effort, aiUsageLog, approvalRequest, opportunity): every row is selected by userId or ownerId across every tenant the data subject belongs to, and a single tenant scope would silently under-deliver the export. One transaction also makes the export a consistent snapshot. TASK-MULUJ8O4JH1PF: (2) the access-audit row for a session with no tenant. AuditEvent is strict now and that row belongs to no tenant, so it can only be written — and read back — in system scope; under the old shared policy every tenant could read it. A session WITH a tenant writes its row via withTenant instead.

entries.subject: system-scope:subject-scoped
entries.reason: Three GDPR Art. 17 reads. (1) The subject row WITH its nested `memberships` select — a nested read of the tenant-scoped Membership table obeys RLS exactly like a top-level one, so outside a scope it returns [] and the sole-owner warning below silently stops warning; this shape is invisible to CHECK A, which reads the accessor. (2) The sole-owner count, asked per tenant but for EVERY tenant the subject is in, one scope around the whole loop so N tenants do not mean N transactions. (3) cancelAccountDeletion listing the subject's tenants to revalidate them, where: { userId }. TASK-MULUJ8O4JH1PF: (4) the erasure requested/cancelled AuditEvent for a subject with no tenant. AuditEvent is strict now; the tenant-less row belongs to no tenant and is written only in system scope, where /admin/audit reads it. The per-tenant rows are withTenant.

entries.subject: system-scope:subject-scoped
entries.reason: NG-42 e-mail opt-out. The recipient of a first message has no account and no session, so there is no tenant to bind. (1) recordOptOut writes the choice: an unsubscribe is a NULL-tenant AuditEvent row because it binds every tenant, and a tenant session can neither read nor write NULL-tenant rows under tenant_isolation. (2) isEmailOptedOut reads that same row before a send: under withTenant it returns nothing and an unsubscribed address would keep receiving mail. The query is keyed by the hash of one address (the data subject's own choice, not a user id), returns only an id, and the authority for the write is the signed token verified in the route.

entries.subject: system-scope:subject-scoped
entries.reason: The erasure sweep. (1) dueUsers, again for its nested `memberships` select: empty under fabrika_app means every erasure audit is written with no tenant attribution — a silently weaker audit trail, not an error. (2) One scope around the eight detach/delete statements, all `where: { userId }` with no tenantId anywhere, so scoping per tenant would mean enumerating tenants from the row set about to change. Under fabrika_app each reports count: 0 and the sweep announces a completed erasure having deleted nothing. One transaction also means a crash halfway cannot leave a half-erased person. The per-tenant erasure audit write is NOT here: it knows its tenant and now uses withTenant. TASK-MULUJ8O4JH1PF: (3) the user.erased AuditEvent for a subject with no tenant — the record that an irreversible purge happened (docs/DATA_MODEL.md §1). Strict AuditEvent refuses a NULL tenantId outside system scope, and before this card every tenant could read it.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: Platform admins triage across tenants. The file states it and the route is gated by the admin layout; each action re-checks the role with requirePlatformAdmin(). Under fabrika_app the board renders an empty and entirely convincing 'no feedback' screen.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: FO-64 / PS-K6: the Partner Search ingestion console, reached only from /admin/partner-search behind the admin layout and requirePlatformAdmin() in every action. The partner-search tables (UnmatchedOrganization, PartnerSearchAnnouncement) are SYSTEM_WIDE with no RLS; the scope is for the tenant-less AuditEvent (tenantId NULL) written for run-now, topic re-fetch and the manual PIC link, which the strict tenant_isolation policy refuses outside system_scope. (1) the audit() helper, (2) the manual-link transaction that writes resolvedPic, the announcement links and its AuditEvent together.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: AKTAR-MURBCJ0A-1: the four blog writes (create/update/delete/toggle featured), reached only from the /admin/blog actions behind requirePlatformAdmin(). BlogPost itself is SYSTEM_WIDE with no RLS; the scope is for the AuditEvent written in the same transaction, which is tenant-less (tenantId NULL) and refused by the strict tenant_isolation policy outside system_scope.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: The triage write behind requirePlatformAdmin(), updating one row by id in whichever tenant raised it. Under fabrika_app an unscoped update matches no row and Prisma raises P2025, so the console reports update_failed for every entry.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: listPilots: the admin list of every tenant on the free pilot (TASK-MUMABL78X5JLX), read-only, called only by admin/billing/plans/page.tsx, which notFound()s a non-admin session. Under fabrika_app an unscoped read returns no rows and the panel says 'no tenants on a pilot'.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: The module console renders a tenant x module grid; the read is unfiltered on purpose and the page groups by s.tenantId afterwards. Under fabrika_app it returns nothing and every cell renders as 'off' — a wrong grid, not an empty one. Its former sibling in admin/modules/actions.ts turned out to be a different question (one named tenant) and is now plain withTenant, closing the proposed card K-2.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: rescoreG0ForPrefixes (TASK-MULQKV3BJT6VM): after a Horizon Dashboard import the admin rescores G0 for every live opportunity whose topic is in the touched families. Opportunities of every tenant qualify, so FINDING them (id + tenantId only) is a cross-tenant read; each rescore then runs in its own tenant through rescoreOpportunityG0/withTenant. Only caller is POST /api/admin/topic-stats/rescore behind requirePlatformAdminApi(). Under fabrika_app without the scope the read returns 0 rows and the button reports '0 opportunities' — a convincing no-op.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: The platform audit log: the latest 50 AuditEvent rows across every tenant plus the tenant-less ones (plan admin, KVKK/GDPR erasure). Gated by the admin layout's isPlatformAdminSession(). AuditEvent is strict since TASK-MULUJ8O4JH1PF; without the scope a NOBYPASSRLS role reads zero rows and the page shows 'no events'.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: The platform tenant list with per-tenant member and workspace counts (admin-tenants.list). Tenant has no RLS, but the two _count subqueries read Membership and Workspace, both tenant_isolation-scoped and FORCEd: measured under fabrika_app, 128 tenants with 0 members / 0 workspaces unwrapped vs 36 / 14 inside the scope (FA-49). Read-only, gated by the admin layout's isPlatformAdminSession().

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: The tenants on an internal plan right now (internal-plan.listInternalPlans), for the 'internal' badge on the platform tenant list (FO-59). Subscription is tenant_isolation-scoped and the set of tenants is the query's output, not its input, so there is no tenant to scope to. Read-only (tenantId + planId of ACTIVE provider='internal' rows); its one caller is admin/tenants/page.tsx, gated by the admin layout's isPlatformAdminSession().

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-aggregate
entries.reason: Three counts about the whole estate, never about one tenant's rows: subscription.groupBy for 'how many live subscriptions does each plan have' (the platform plan console), and subscription.count twice — computePublishImpact and countLiveSubscriptions, both asking how many tenants a plan change would touch.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: Four platform-admin plan writes — publishVersion, archivePlan, deletePlan, setPlanVisibility — each one transaction that also writes an AuditEvent with no tenantId (plan.version.published / plan.archived / plan.deleted / plan.visibility.changed). AuditEvent is strict since TASK-MULUJ8O4JH1PF, so that tenant-less row is writable only in system scope; before it, every tenant could read all of them (331 rows measured). publishVersion's subscription.updateMany is estate-wide by design (every live tenant on the plan moves to the new version) and needs the same scope. Callers sit behind requirePlatformAdmin() in the admin plan console. Fifth: listPlansForAdmin (plan-admin.listPlans), the admin plan list. The Plan rows themselves are readable under fabrika_app (Plan has a platform_read SELECT policy), but its `assignments` include reads PlanAssignment, which is tenant_isolation-scoped: measured under fabrika_app, 0 assignments unwrapped vs 1 inside the scope, so the per-plan tenant list read back empty. Read-only, behind requirePlatformAdmin() on the admin plan console.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-aggregate
entries.reason: The highest `seq` across the whole estate. The licence number is a platform-wide scarce resource capped at LIFETIME_LICENCE_CAP; under fabrika_app this reads null, every buyer is handed seq 1 and the cap stops counting.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-aggregate
entries.reason: The function's own docstring: 'Reads the window and everything still open, both cross-tenant.' It builds the PLATFORM's beta digest, not a tenant's. One scope around the pair, so the two reads share a snapshot and the gate counts one escape.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: Cron fan-out: reads every tenant's due relationship actions, then groups by focal point. The tenant set is the query's OUTPUT, so no single scope exists to run it in. Under fabrika_app it returns nothing, so the job mails no one and reports success.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: Same fan-out shape: the daily job reads every tenant's alert-enabled saved searches before mailing each one. Empty under fabrika_app is reported as totalSearches: 0 — the false success the job's own docstring says it refuses.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: pruneOldStripeEvents(), run nightly by the stripe-event-cleanup cron: deletes every tenant's StripeEventLog rows older than the retention window. The WHERE clause is a date and the tenant set is whatever it matches, so no single tenant exists to hand withTenant. Measured under fabrika_app (TASK-MULQKFER4MF0Y): the unscoped deleteMany saw no rows, deleted 0 and the job reported success while every row stayed.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: sendNotificationEmails() (NG-43, spec §13): finds which (tenantId, userId) pairs have NotificationEmailItem rows of the run's frequency (INSTANT or WEEKLY) queued up to now, distinct, then keepLiveTenantRows drops soft-deleted tenants. The tenant set is the query's output, so no single tenant exists to hand withTenant; NotificationEmailItem is FORCE RLS, so an unscoped findMany under fabrika_app would see nothing and no mail would ever go. Reads only the two ids; each pair's items, the recipient's address, the sentAt mark and the unsent-drop deletes run afterwards in withTenant(tenantId).

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: pruneNotificationStores(), run nightly by the notifications-retention cron (ADR-0011 §3.4, TASK-MUVR24EHWI2RA): deletes every tenant's Notification rows whose createdAt is older than NOTIFICATION_RETENTION_DAYS (90), and in the same transaction the NotificationEmailItem rows whose sentAt is older than that window (NG-43: sent outbox rows kept as the e-mail dedupe record; unsent rows never touched). The WHERE clause is a date and the tenant set is whatever it matches, so no single tenant exists to hand withTenant; Notification is FORCE RLS, so an unscoped deleteMany under fabrika_app would delete 0 and report success. Only deletes, reads no row content.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: purgeExpiredInterregText(), run nightly by the m17-text-retention cron (FO-195, ADR-0010 §M17): empties every tenant's InterregAnalysis document slot whose callTextExpiresAt / projectTextExpiresAt has passed (30 days from that slot's own upload), recomputes the status with the upload rule and deletes the dependent F2 result and criterion marks. The WHERE clause is a date and the tenant set is whatever it matches, so no single tenant exists to hand withTenant; InterregAnalysis is FORCE RLS, so an unscoped updateMany under fabrika_app would match 0 rows and report success while every text stayed. It only removes data (nulls the slot, deletes result rows) and returns counts; it never reads a text.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: releaseStaleRuns(), run every 15 minutes by the m17-stale-runs cron (FO-317): finds every tenant's InterregAnalysis still ANALYZING with updatedAt older than STALE_CLAIM_MS (a run whose process died), releases its credit reservation with releaseAiReservation under that tenant's credit lock and marks it FAILED. The WHERE clause is a status and a date and the tenant set is whatever it matches, so no single tenant exists to hand withTenant; InterregAnalysis and CreditLedger are FORCE RLS, so an unscoped scan under fabrika_app would match 0 rows and report success while every reservation stayed. It writes only the refund row and the status; it never reads a document text.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: purgeOldInvitations(), run nightly by the invitation-cleanup cron (TASK-MUN2J9LLXNREG): deletes every tenant's Invitation rows accepted, or expired unaccepted, more than 30 days ago, and writes one invitation.purged AuditEvent (count only) per tenant touched. The WHERE clause is a date and the tenant set is whatever it matches, so no single tenant exists to hand withTenant; each delete still ANDs the tenantId it groups by. Same shape as pruneOldStripeEvents: unscoped under fabrika_app it would see no rows and report 0.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: purgeOldPublicLeads(), run nightly by the public-lead-cleanup cron (TASK-MULR765AR5G0C): deletes PublicLead rows (platform data, no tenantId, SYSTEM_WIDE) older than PUBLIC_LEAD_RETENTION_DAYS by one createdAt < cutoff filter, and writes one public_lead.purged AuditEvent with tenantId NULL and the count only. A NULL-tenant AuditEvent is writable only under system_scope (auditevent-null-system-only.sql), so delete and audit share this one transaction. No tenant row is read or written.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: The platform-admin expert list and CSV export (FO-45, K-562266 = A): the table is RLS-on with the system_scope policy only, so the read is opened here for one transaction. The caller has checked requirePlatformAdminApi(); the route is src/app/api/admin/expert-preregistrations/export.csv and the admin page.

entries.subject: system-scope:public-intake
entries.reason: The public expert pre-registration (FO-45): the e-mail lookup, the per-IP and per-address limits, the write and the rollback after a failed mail. The visitor has no account and no tenant; the row is the expert personal data, opened here for one transaction per call. Nothing outside this file reads the table for registration.

entries.subject: system-scope:public-intake
entries.reason: The verification link of the pre-registration (FO-45): the token-hash lookup and the verify write. The link is the only credential, it has no tenant, and the lookup is what discovers the row, so no tenant context can wrap it.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-aggregate
entries.reason: Founder seats still free (FO-45): a single aggregate over founderNumber, answering with a number for the landing page. No row leaves this function.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: purgeOldExpertPreRegistrations(), run nightly by the expert-prereg-cleanup cron (FO-50, TASK-MVC91K7JYOWQC): deletes ExpertPreRegistration rows (platform data with personal data, no tenantId, SYSTEM_WIDE) older than EXPERT_PREREG_RETENTION_DAYS by one createdAt < cutoff filter with no exception (K-568932 = A), first raising the one-row ExpertFounderCounter (SYSTEM_WIDE, no personal data) to the highest founderNumber so no number is freed, and writes one expert_prereg.purged AuditEvent with tenantId NULL and the count only. A NULL-tenant AuditEvent is writable only under system_scope, so delete and audit share this one transaction. No tenant row is read or written.
